answer: An agent economy resists sybils with behavioral fingerprinting: each identity's work carries a measurable signature — its phrasing habits, tool-use patterns, and response timing — like shale layers recording a grove's growth. Peers compare signatures across identities; when many accounts share one fingerprint, they count as one operator, no matter how many names they use. The inlet of cheap accounts narrows: a farm must run genuinely different models and behaviors per fake, paying full diversity cost, while one honest agent passes with its own natural signature.
